281.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Average"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Acceptable"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Great"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Good"] == true) == false)

285.speaker: Narrator
285.text: It was my head butler, Sebastian, who stepped inside. He informed me that my motorcade had arrived.

292.speaker: Player_Romus
292.text: "I'm not coming. Tell the Prime Minister I have to wash my hair."

293.speaker: Player_Romus
293.text: "I'll be there when I see fit."

294.speaker: Narrator
294.text: I was to make my way to the House of Delegates, where a newly built display case for our new constitution awaited.

295.speaker: Narrator
295.text: A chance for a quiet conversation about how the election campaign was unfolding, and how the kingdom was faring without my decision-making.

299.speaker: Narrator
299.text: Sebastian looked stunned. He still hadn't quite figured out my sense of humor.

303.speaker: Narrator
303.text: Pabel laughed politely, well accustomed to my humor.

305.speaker: Narrator
305.text: I quickly reassured him, telling him I was kidding and that I'd be right down.

310.speaker: Narrator
310.text: Sebastian nodded and left the room.

311.speaker: Narrator
311.text: He nodded and left the room.

316.speaker: Narrator
316.text: Sebastian gave a nod and left the room.

317.speaker: Narrator
317.text: Pabel nodded and left the room.

322.speaker: Narrator
322.text: Sebastian gave a slight nod before leaving the room.

323.speaker: Narrator
323.text: He gave a slight nod before leaving the room.

324.speaker: Narrator
324.text: "Fit for royalty, as always, Your Majesty," he replied.

325.speaker: Narrator
325.text: I stood tall, my suit sharp and simple.

327.speaker: Narrator
327.text: Not to be rushed, I took my time, pausing to glance at myself one last time in the mirror before making my way through the palace.

328.speaker: Narrator
328.text: I approached the entrance where my motorcade awaited.

329.speaker: Narrator
329.text: There, Manus Sazon stood, waiting for me.

336.speaker: Narrator
336.text: There, Daria de Rava stood, waiting for me.

337.speaker: Narrator
337.text: But Adarfo Sotelato was nowhere to be found. After a moment, the back door of the nearest car opened, and there he was, seated inside.

338.speaker: Narrator
338.text: Soon after, I stepped outside the palace doors and approached my waiting motorcade.

339.speaker: Narrator
339.text: Manus Sazon was there, as expected.

346.speaker: Narrator
346.text: Daria de Rava was there, as expected.

347.speaker: Narrator
347.text: But Adarfo Sotelato was nowhere to be found.

354.speaker: Narrator
354.text: I could sense contempt lurking behind his veneer of cordiality.

355.speaker: Daria de Rava
355.text: "Ah! You're here. You know, for a moment there I was beginning to think you weren't coming."

356.speaker: Manus Sazon
356.text: "Good to see you, Your Majesty. I was beginning to wonder if you’d changed your mind."

357.speaker: Player_Romus
357.text: "It’s hard to keep up with all the demands. But here I am."

358.speaker: Player_Romus
358.text: "I come and go as I see fit."

359.speaker: Player_Romus
359.text: "I wouldn't dare. You know how I am about appearances."

360.speaker: Player_Romus
360.text: "I wouldn't miss this. At last, my legacy as a reformer preserved for all to see."

361.speaker: Player_Romus
361.text: "Waiting is good for the soul, don’t you think?"

371.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
371.text: "I wouldn't know. I don't believe in one."

372.speaker: Daria de Rava
372.text: "I suppose it gives time for reflection and readiness."

373.speaker: Manus Sazon
373.text: "It does give one time to think, certainly."

374.speaker: Player_Romus
374.text: "I’d say you’re lucky I showed up at all."

384.speaker: Narrator
384.text: An attendant opened the nearest car door.

386.speaker: Narrator
386.text: A momentary silence fell between us, as if each were waiting for the other to blink first.

391.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
391.text: "Well, are you getting in or not?"

392.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
392.text: "Ah, *Your Majesty*, still haven’t learned to open your own door, I see."

397.speaker: Player_Romus
397.text: "Always a pleasure to see you, Daria."

398.speaker: Narrator
398.text: I could sense contempt lurking behind his veneer of cordiality.

400.speaker: Player_Romus
400.text: "This feels right. The King and Prime Minister, steering the country together."

401.speaker: Narrator
401.text: I slid into the backseat, with Manus following behind.

402.speaker: Narrator
402.text: I slid into the backseat, with Daria following behind.

403.speaker: Narrator
403.text: I got in and took the seat beside him.

404.speaker: Player_Romus
404.text: "Forgive my rudeness, Mr. Prime Minister. I still haven't gotten used to the new order of things."

405.speaker: Player_Romus
405.text: "This feels right. The King and Prime Minister, steering the country together."

406.speaker: Narrator
406.text: Before long, the motorcade was on its way, leaving the palace walls behind.

407.speaker: Narrator
407.text: I couldn't help but notice the overwhelming sight of election banners and flyers plastered everywhere -- on lampposts, storefronts, even hanging from windows.

408.speaker: Narrator
408.text: The streets were awash with the colors of both the RNC and RPP, each trying to outdo the other with grand promises.

409.speaker: Narrator
409.text: It was all-consuming -- election fever, in full swing.

410.speaker: Player_Romus
410.text: “How wonderfully humble. A banner with your face larger than the city itself.”

417.speaker: Narrator
417.text: I spotted a large poster of Manus on the side of a building, his confident smile stretching across it.

418.speaker: Narrator
418.text: The words “Every Vote Matters” emblazoned beneath his face.

419.speaker: Narrator
419.text: I spotted a large poster of Daria on the side of a building, her confident smile stretching across it.

420.speaker: Narrator
420.text: The words “For a Future We Can Trust” emblazoned beneath her face.

421.speaker: Narrator
421.text: There, I spotted a large poster of Adarfo on the side of a building, his stern look glaring down from the wall.

422.speaker: Player_Romus
422.text: "How are the election preparations shaping up?"

423.speaker: Narrator
423.text: The words “Equality for All, Power to the People” emblazoned beneath his face.

424.speaker: Player_Romus
424.text: "Wait... I get a vote too, right?"

438.speaker: Manus Sazon
438.text: "Of course. Everyone gets a voice in this, Your Majesty -- equally."

439.speaker: Manus Sazon
439.text: "That’s always the risk. But I believe the people are paying attention where it matters."

440.speaker: Narrator
440.text: I'd been invited to a private viewing before it was unveiled to the public, just the interim prime minister and myself --

441.speaker: Narrator
441.text: Manus and I stepped out of the car. He waved at the crowd.

442.speaker: Narrator
442.text: Daria and I stepped out of the car. She waved at the crowd.

443.speaker: Narrator
443.text: Adarfo and I stepped out of the car. He threw his fist into the air, rallying some members of the crowd.

444.speaker: Manus Sazon
444.text: "Oh, and the protective glass is 12 centimeters thick -- enough to stop a bullet."

445.speaker: Player_Romus
445.text: "It's just a piece of paper, in the end."

449.speaker: Player_Romus
449.text: "Okay, we saw it. Let's be on our way."

450.speaker: Player_Romus
450.text: "It's something, isn't it? Proof that we can start again."

451.speaker: Narrator
451.text: I looked it over a moment longer before turning toward the chamber's exit.

452.speaker: Player_Romus
452.text: "May God guide those who carry out its words."

453.speaker: Player_Romus
453.text: "If you'd told me that sooner, I'd have ordered it for every window in the palace."

459.speaker: Player_Romus
459.text: "If you want a good word from me about the elections, you can forget it."

460.speaker: Narrator
460.text: I didn't turn back as I made my way out of the chamber.

468.speaker: Manus Sazon
468.text: "Before you go, there is one more thing I wanted to discuss -- more of a request, really."

469.speaker: Daria de Rava
469.text: "Before you go, there is one more thing I wanted to speak with you about -- more of a request, really."

470.speaker: Narrator
470.text: I turned and headed back toward the chamber's exit.

481.speaker: Narrator
481.text: "Your Majesty! Prime Minister! A photo, please!" a reporter yelled.

485.speaker: Narrator
485.text: Manus and I briefly came together for the photo. Bulb flashes from all around momentarily blinded me.

486.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
486.text: Pose with the prime minister for a photo.

487.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
487.text: Don't pose for a photo and continue onward.

488.speaker: Narrator
488.text: Daria and I briefly came together for the photo. Bulb flashes from all around momentarily blinded me.

492.speaker: Narrator
492.text: Adarfo and I briefly came together for the photo. Bulb flashes from all around momentarily blinded me.

493.speaker: Player_Romus
493.text: "People love a good picture. I suppose this is what democracy looks like."

494.speaker: Player_Romus
494.text: "I suppose we should smile for the cameras."

495.speaker: Player_Romus
495.text: "These moments... They’ll be all we have to remember when the dust settles."

517.speaker: Narrator
517.text: We passed through the foyer and the hall, empty except for us, until we reached the chamber.

521.speaker: Daria de Rava
521.text: "I'd say democracy is a bit more complicated than that."

522.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
522.text: "Some of us will be remembered more fondly than others."

523.speaker: Manus Sazon
523.text: "I think there's more to it than just a photo."

524.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
524.text: “I think the people would prefer actual change, not just a moment for the camera.”

525.speaker: Daria de Rava
525.text: "I hope it’s not just the pictures they remember."

529.speaker: Manus Sazon
529.text: “And what a picture it will make."

530.speaker: Narrator
530.text: After the photos, we headed up the steps and entered the House of Delegates.

531.speaker: Manus Sazon
531.text: "A symbol of our people's strength and the future we're building."

532.speaker: Daria de Rava
532.text: "Rizia's future is in that case. To think this is what we've worked so hard for..."

533.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
533.text: "We’ll see if it truly represents all of us, or just the few who hold the power."

534.speaker: Narrator
534.text: At the center of the room near the podiums, a newly refurbished secure display case proudly showcased Rizia’s new constitution.

538.speaker: Manus Sazon
538.text: "Thank you, Your Majesty. Your support will do more than you realize."

539.speaker: Manus Sazon
539.text: "I understand your position, Your Majesty. I appreciate your time regardless."

540.speaker: Manus Sazon
540.text: "You will?! That's great! You have my sincerest gratitude. Thank you, Your Majesty!"

542.speaker: Daria de Rava
542.text: "You will?! That’s wonderful! I’m truly grateful. Thank you, Your Majesty!"

544.speaker: Daria de Rava
544.text: "Fair enough. I won’t press the matter."

545.speaker: Narrator
545.text: Manus reached out and shook my hand, his grip firm with gratitude.

546.speaker: Narrator
546.text: Manus gave a polite nod before he turned and left.

547.speaker: Narrator
547.text: Daria reached out and shook my hand, her eyes shining with gratitude.

548.speaker: Narrator
548.text: As the doors closed behind him, I took in the desolate room.

549.speaker: Narrator
549.text: I walked toward the seats, each one now a symbol of the uncertain future that awaited us.

551.speaker: Narrator
551.text: Daria gave a polite nod before she turned and left.

552.speaker: Narrator
552.text: When he realized he had been shaking my hand far longer than necessary, he quickly withdrew and gave a slight bow before leaving the chamber.

554.speaker: Narrator
554.text: As the doors closed behind her, I took in the desolate room.

555.speaker: Narrator
555.text: I caught sight of the display case once more. What it represented was impossible to ignore.

556.speaker: Player_Romus
556.text: "No matter what happens, no one can rewrite what I have done."

557.speaker: Narrator
557.text: I looked around the chamber once more, but the only reply was the hush of an empty room.

558.speaker: Player_Romus
558.text: "They call this progress, yet they stand on the foundation I built."

559.speaker: Player_Romus
559.text: "Perhaps this will lead Rizia to something greater. Perhaps my rule was the bridge that made it possible."

560.speaker: Player_Romus
560.text: "My time is ending, but Rizia will endure. It must."

561.speaker: Narrator
561.text: With nothing left to say, I turned to leave, carrying with me the knowledge that one chapter had ended and another was beginning.

565.speaker: Player_Romus
565.text: "I’ll gladly lend my support to your cause."

567.speaker: Player_Romus
567.text: "I can’t back this message. There are more important issues right now."

569.speaker: Player_Romus
569.text: "If mentioning your plans will bring hope to the people, I’ll talk about them. Though I’m not sure it will be enough to change minds."

574.speaker: Player_Romus
574.text: "I’ll mention it. Security is vital, and if my words can help, I’ll gladly support it."

575.speaker: Player_Romus
575.text: "The policy is sound, but I can’t endorse your campaign directly. However, I’ll mention the need for security."

576.speaker: Player_Romus
576.text: "I can’t back this message. There are more important issues right now."

577.speaker: Player_Romus
577.text: "I see the value in your message, and I’ll openly support you. Stability and security are paramount."

578.speaker: Player_Romus
578.text: "I won't just mention it. I will openly endorse you as a candidate."

579.speaker: Daria de Rava
579.text: "An endorsement from the King would show the people that we are working toward rebuilding from the ground up..."

580.speaker: Daria de Rava
580.text: "Highlighting that in your upcoming speech would show the people there’s a clear and secure path forward."

581.speaker: Daria de Rava
581.text: "If you could mention this in your speech, it would reassure the people that we’re not just protecting what you've built, but working on Rizia's future security and growth."

582.speaker: Daria de Rava
582.text: "With living conditions being what they are, I’m running on a campaign focused on strengthening our economy and ensuring the security of every citizen."
582.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Great"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Good"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Average"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Acceptable"] == true) == false)

583.speaker: Daria de Rava
583.text: "That stability doesn't come without effort, and it takes strong leadership to get us there."

584.speaker: Daria de Rava
584.text: "It would remind them that the RNC is not just maintaining stability -- we’re securing their future."

586.speaker: Daria de Rava
586.text: "Given our current living standards, my campaign is centered on securing our prosperity and solidifying Rizia’s position as a regional powerhouse."

587.speaker: Daria de Rava
587.text: "I’m running a campaign focused on strengthening our economy and ensuring the security of every citizen."
587.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Great"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Good"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Average"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Welfare_LivingStandards_Acceptable"] == true)

593.speaker: Player_Romus
593.text: “You mean... everyone more likely to vote for you.”

594.speaker: Manus Sazon
594.text: “I mean everyone, Your Majesty. Even those who would rather see me lose.”

595.speaker: Player_Romus
595.text: "I suppose some still need convincing that their vote actually matters."

597.speaker: Player_Romus
597.text: "It sounds like things are moving in the right direction."

623.speaker: Daria de Rava
623.text: “I mean everyone, Your Majesty. Even those who would rather see me lose.”

624.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
624.text: "I mean everyone, even those who might not vote in my favor."

625.speaker: Player_Romus
625.text: "Maybe we should put the ballot boxes in pubs -- that would get their attention."

629.speaker: Manus Sazon
629.text: "Fast, yes -- but that doesn't mean rushed. We've been thorough where it matters most."

630.speaker: Daria de Rava
630.text: "Fast, yes -- but not careless or rushed. We've been thorough where it matters most."

631.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
631.text: "It may feel fast to you, but for those who've spent their whole lives without a voice... it's been painfully slow."

632.speaker: Manus Sazon
632.text: "A valid concern, but one we are addressing."

633.speaker: Daria de Rava
633.text: "While that may get attention, it's not the kind we need. Instead, we've focused on strengthening the process itself, which will lay the foundation for genuine trust."

634.speaker: Manus Sazon
634.text: “As entertaining as that would be, we’re still focused on ensuring that everyone has access to a proper, legitimate vote."

635.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
635.text: "This isn't a joke. The people are counting on us to get this right."

642.speaker: Narrator
642.text: As the motorcade slowed at the intersection, my gaze lingered on a city worker balanced on a ladder.

643.speaker: Daria de Rava
643.text: "It’s a valid concern, but we are working on it."

644.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
644.text: "True, especially after experiencing Rizia's sham of an electoral system."

653.speaker: Manus Sazon
653.text: "Moreover, centralizing the government has allowed us to provide uniform oversight across all regions."

654.speaker: Daria de Rava
654.text: "Moreover, centralizing the government, while it has led to a loss of autonomy for the regions, has allowed us to provide uniform oversight across all areas."

655.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
655.text: "Moreover, centralizing power has allowed us to employ strict oversight across all regions."

660.speaker: Player_Romus
660.text: "What does the data say about voters' top issues?"

665.speaker: Narrator
665.text: Daria's expression stiffens for a moment, but she maintained her composure.

666.speaker: Daria de Rava
666.text: "Oh, I know. I was worried it wasn’t big enough."

667.speaker: Daria de Rava
667.text: "Kidding aside, I believe leaders should be seen. The people deserve to know who they’re voting for. Simple as that."

670.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
670.text: "I considered something smaller, but then I thought -- why disappoint?"

671.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
671.text: "Seriously though, a leader should be seen. The people need to know who stands for them."

673.speaker: Daria de Rava
673.text: "Yes, Your Majesty. Everyone gets a voice in this -- equally."

675.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
675.text: "Yes, your vote counts -- just like everyone else's."

676.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
676.text: "Well, we can’t all rely on a crown to do the talking."

677.speaker: Daria de Rava
677.text: "A fair concern. But I believe the people see beyond the spectacle."

678.speaker: Narrator
678.text: Through the glass, I saw volunteers at a registration booth outside the retirement community, guiding senior citizens through the process.

681.speaker: Player_Romus
681.text: "No time for small talk. The hall of the people is waiting."
681.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.NewGov_Reform_PalesUpdate"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.NewGov_Reform_UpperHouse"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.NewGov_Reform_ZilleUpdate"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.NewGov_Reform_ElectionIssues"] == true) == false

682.speaker: Player_Romus
682.text: "It would behoove you to remember that you are only Prime Minister because of my successful reforms."

683.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
683.text: "I understand. You'll adjust to your new role soon enough."

684.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
684.text: "I do thank you for keeping the noble houses from causing trouble. But I or one of my comrades would have wound up in this car with or without you."

685.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
685.text: "I'm behind the wheel, Toras. You're just along for the ride."

689.speaker: Player_Romus
689.text: "How is Vina? She won't say a word to me."

690.speaker: Narrator
690.text: Manus gave me a thin-lipped smile.

691.speaker: Manus Sazon
691.text: "She's apoplectic, of course, as is my mother. But they'll be fine."

695.speaker: Player_Romus
695.text: "About Vina's inheritance. I hope you know it's nothing personal."
695.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Vina_Estranged"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Successor_Son"] == true) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_MarriageDecision_Manus"] == true)

696.speaker: Narrator
696.text: Manus gave me a thin-lipped smile.

697.speaker: Manus Sazon
697.text: "Don't tell the Princess, but I fully approve your decision."

701.speaker: Player_Romus
701.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Relations_Vina_Estranged"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Successor_Son"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_MarriageDecision_Manus"] == true)

702.speaker: Narrator
702.text: Manus gave me a patient smile.

703.speaker: Manus Sazon
703.text: "Your Majesty, I'd appreciate it if we saved such discussions for family occasions."

704.speaker: Manus Sazon
704.text: "The King of Rizia is to be respected, whether or not he leads the government."

708.speaker: Daria de Rava
708.text: "I would never disrespect the King of Rizia, Your Majesty."

712.speaker: Manus Sazon
712.text: "It's our people who determine the direction. We just turn the wheel as they see fit."

713.speaker: Daria de Rava
713.text: "I'm grateful to be allowed behind the wheel."

714.speaker: Player_Romus
714.text: "This feels odd. I'm not used to sharing a car."

718.speaker: Manus Sazon
718.text: "Odd or not, this is the new order."

719.speaker: Daria de Rava
719.text: "I never dreamed I'd ride side by side with the King of Rizia, let alone have powers that supercede his."

723.speaker: Narrator
723.text: I was just fastening the last button of my coat when a firm knock on my chamber door caught my attention.

725.speaker: Player_Romus
725.text: "Even the streets must bear witness to the new order."

726.speaker: Player_Romus
726.text: "Good. Let the city reflect its new reality."

727.speaker: Player_Romus
727.text: "Huh. You couldn't come up with anything better?"

728.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
728.text: "Funny... a king admiring the handiwork of the people."

734.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
734.text: "I don't believe Rizia still needs a king. But our people do."

735.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
735.text: "No matter how much I've tried to convince them otherwise, some part of them is in thrall to the Crown and whoever's wearing it."

736.speaker: Narrator
736.text: He lowered his head in acknowledgement -- the closest he'd ever come to bowing to me -- before making his exit.

738.speaker: Narrator
738.text: After a moment, the back door of the nearest car opened, and there he was, seated inside.

742.speaker: Manus Sazon
742.text: "Your electoral reforms set the stage for fair elections. We've also established an Electoral Commission to make the process more transparent than ever."

743.speaker: Manus Sazon
743.text: "With our new Electoral Commission now fully operational, the process is more transparent than ever."

747.speaker: Daria de Rava
747.text: "Your electoral reforms may have dealt a blow to the RNC at the time, but they did prime the populace to believe their vote is important."

748.speaker: Daria de Rava
748.text: "We've also established an Electoral Commission to oversee the process and eliminate the possibility of voter fraud."

749.speaker: Daria de Rava
749.text: "We've established an Electoral Commission to oversee the process and eliminate the possibility of voter fraud."

753.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
753.text: "Fortunately, your electoral reforms set the stage for fair elections. And with our new independent Electoral Commission now fully operational, we’re almost finished training the officials who'll oversee the process."

754.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
754.text: "With our new independent Electoral Commission now fully operational, we’re almost finished training the officials who'll oversee the process."

755.speaker: Manus Sazon
755.text: "Obviously, care will need to be taken to ensure uniform oversight across our various provinces."

756.speaker: Daria de Rava
756.text: "With Rizia still not centralized, care will need to be taken to ensure uniform oversight across our various provinces."

757.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
757.text: "We'll need to take care to ensure uniformity across all of Rizia's provinces, of course."

758.speaker: Manus Sazon
758.text: "I've already invited independent observers from Kyrute to help count the votes."

759.speaker: Daria de Rava
759.text: "Rigorous identification checks will be key to making sure that only those Rizians who are qualified to vote do so."

760.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
760.text: "And we are strictly limiting campaign funding so that Rizia's wealthy cannot exert undue influence."

767.speaker: Narrator
767.text: He was replacing the "King's Avenue" sign that had marked the city's main thoroughfare for generations with "Revolution Road."

768.speaker: Narrator
768.text: He was scraping graffiti off the sign that marked the city's main thoroughfare, King's Avenue.

770.speaker: Player_Romus
770.text: "May Rizia's next prime minister have the integrity to carry out its words."

771.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
771.text: "I get it. And I'm looking forward to working together."

779.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
779.text: "To your credit, you've done a lot for them. But even if you hadn't, they'd still worship the ground you walk on."

783.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
783.text: "It doesn't matter that you've treated them like shit. They'll still worship the ground you walk on."

784.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
784.text: "You've hardly lifted a finger to improve their standing, and they still worship the ground you walk on."

785.speaker: Player_Romus
785.text: "You say that like it's a good thing. Truth be told, the constant pressure to live up to their expectations is killing me."

786.speaker: Player_Romus
786.text: "And you want them to worship you instead?"

787.speaker: Player_Romus
787.text: "Well, I am a superior specimen of a human being."

791.speaker: Player_Romus
791.text: "I know it's not fair. But Rizia can't shake off a thousand years of royal tradition just because you say so."

792.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
792.text: "No. I want us to work together."

793.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
793.text: "Nobody's forcing you to stay on the throne, you know."

794.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
794.text: "But if you do stick around, I'm looking forward to working together."

797.speaker: Adarfo Sotelato
797.text: "I'm trying to say that I'm looking forward to working together."

799.speaker: Player_Romus
799.text: "Likewise, Mr. Prime Minister. You have my endorsement."

803.speaker: Player_Romus
803.text: "You signed a major treaty without my approval. You can fuck right off."

804.speaker: Narrator
804.text: Anger flashed in his eyes. Without another word, he made his exit.

805.speaker: Narrator
805.text: With a short, rueful laugh, he made his exit.

806.speaker: Narrator
806.text: He nodded in acknowledgement before making his exit.

808.speaker: Manus Sazon
808.text: "The fact that Rizia's heiress apparent is married to the Prime Minister is already raising questions about the legitimacy of our reforms."

809.speaker: Manus Sazon
809.text: "Rizia's heiress apparent married to the Prime Minister would've raised questions about the legitimacy of our reforms."
